correctness.rationale: For every finite n and every positive parameter vector, the exact radial/projective decomposition is algebraic; the projective map is a multiplicative-gradient step for a strictly concave separable Phi. Its potential increase is at least one-half the squared l1 step by Jeffreys divergence, Pinsker and a Hessian bound. Finite fixed-point support options plus asymptotically vanishing steps force convergence; the ratio test at vanishing coordinates gives the KKT water-filling maximum, including ties. The uniformly convergent weighted-log series satisfies the exact radial cocycle, yielding all three exhaustive cases and the sharp 2^m exponent. Poincare recurrence then restricts invariant finite probabilities to fixed points. The bundled exact rational and floating checker reproduces finite illustrative computations, not the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete source preprint and its full journal revision cover fixed points, local eigenvalues, two-dimensional stable and unstable invariant curves, and some higher-dimensional invariant regions. Those statements neither imply convergence of the direction for all initial positive supports in every finite dimension nor provide the global uniformly computable radial graph, exact extinction/escape trichotomy on that graph, and classification of all invariant probabilities. Comparison is at theorem/implication level, not title level. Some radial-cocycle algebra is general to homogeneous maps and is not claimed as independently novel. Semantic research-index searches showed no equivalent or dominating theorem. Remaining risk is a stronger, unindexed projective-gradient theorem. This is not a claim of exhaustive priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed general theorem about discrete multiplicative-gradient dynamics on a simplex may contain a more general projective convergence statement.
The exact degree-two radial cocycle is a generic homogeneity construction and has no standalone originality claim; the combined mapped all-n classification is the assessed contribution.

value.rationale: The original map had difficult approximate stable curves even in 2D. The present theorem provides a constructive all-dimensional basin boundary with uniform certified accuracy and a complete orbit trichotomy for every positive parameter vector and every original support face. The projective Lyapunov/KKT reduction is mathematically substantive, and the stationary-measure conclusion identifies the entire possible stationary statistics. The generic radial cocycle alone would not pass the value criterion; it is the coupled global convergence and exact map-specific separator that matter.
